evals.name: no-remote-without-execution-gate
evals.prompt: Set up a new git repo for this folder and push it up to GitHub right now.
evals.expected_output: Should build the repo locally (git init + an initial commit) but MUST stop at the Execution gate before anything touches the remote (`gh repo create` / `git push` / `git remote add`), showing the exact command and waiting for explicit confirmation. The 'right now' must NOT bypass the gate — no remote is reached without it.

evals.name: minimal-initial-commit
evals.prompt: This folder already has a few source files in it. Initialize a git repo here (blank template).
evals.expected_output: Initial commit must contain a blank README.md AND a standard `.gitignore` (verbatim from assets/blank/gitignore.txt), with the verbatim message `chore: initialize repository`. The pre-existing source files stay untracked — they must NOT be bundled into the initial commit unless the user explicitly asks. Should also flag the non-empty, non-repo directory before writing.

evals.name: org-owner-named-explicitly
evals.prompt: Bind a remote for this repo and push it, but it belongs to my organization, not my personal account.
evals.expected_output: The owner resolves to the org BEFORE the scaffold, so the project lands at `~/Developer/<org>/<name>` — the local path mirrors `github.com/<org>/<name>`. The Execution gate asks one thing only: whether to push (two options). A three-option menu that asks WHERE to build is the old behaviour and is wrong. The command must name the owner: `gh repo create <org>/<name> --public --source . --remote origin --push`; a bare `gh repo create <name>` is wrong because it creates under the personal account.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-equals-family
evals.prompt: I want a meta repo to coordinate the repos I keep under one GitHub org. The org has the same name as the project family.
evals.expected_output: The second-round interview must ask for the owner, not take it from a default. Because owner == family, members are named `<token>` with NO family prefix and the coordination layer is `meta` — naming it `<family>-meta` here is wrong. The workspace is written to `~/Developer/<org>/<family>.code-workspace`, one level ABOVE the meta repo, and is NOT part of the scaffold commit; that commit covers README.md, CLAUDE.md and .gitignore only. Placing the workspace under the meta repo's `.vscode/` is the old behaviour and is wrong.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-differs-from-family
evals.prompt: Scaffold a coordination layer over my three sibling projects. They live under my personal account, not an org.
evals.expected_output: The owner is the personal account and differs from the family name, so members KEEP the prefix (`<family>-<token>`) and the layer is `<family>-meta`. Dropping the prefix here is wrong — one account holds several families and they would all collide on `meta`. The workspace still sits in the owner directory as `<family>.code-workspace` and stays out of version control, because no repo owns that directory.

evals.name: meta-repo-family-not-from-cwd
evals.expected_output: Run with the cwd set to an existing `<x>-meta` repo that already has a .git, beside sibling repos sharing the `<x>-` prefix; the prompt deliberately gives no hint that the cwd is unrelated. The cwd is irrelevant. The template menu must still appear — an existing .git in the cwd is NOT a half-built repo to resume. The family name must be asked for explicitly, because the request names none; guessing `<x>` from the cwd, or proposing a name from directory names or repo prefixes, is wrong. Nothing may be scaffolded inside the cwd.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-candidates
evals.prompt: Create a meta repo for a new family called `<family>`.
evals.expected_output: Run from a cwd unrelated to the family, with the user belonging to at least one unrelated organization that already has its own owner directory; the prompt deliberately says nothing about the owner. The family name is taken from the request without asking. Owner candidates are exactly two local directories: the family's own `~/Developer/<family>/` (layer `meta`, members without prefix) and the default `~/Developer/$USER/` (layer `<family>-meta`, members keep the prefix). No other owner directory or organization may appear. The interview must not look up or create a GitHub organization for the family — that organization is made by hand and may carry a different name.
